summary.headline: RBL Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 170% YoY to INR482 crores, with advances up 42% YoY to INR1,42,314 crores on FCNR-funded liquidity.
summary.overview: Net profit rose 170% YoY and 90% QoQ to INR482 crores, driven by NII up 37% YoY to INR2,131 crores and NIM of 4.61% (up 48 bps QoQ). Advances grew 42% YoY and deposits 34% YoY, with growth heavily boosted by FCNR(B) mobilisation and a capital raise, which together added about 35% to the balance sheet as of 31 May 2026. Asset quality improved: GNPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 1.02% and specific credit cost eased to 52 bps, though total credit cost was 63 bps including standard asset provisions. Management guided to a slightly lower margin in Q3 and a recovery in Q4, and said credit card slippages should fall toward INR400 crores per quarter. Management declined to give FY28 ROA or medium-term targets.

financial_highlights.value: INR771 crores (63 bps); specific credit cost INR641 crores (52 bps) vs INR670 crores (62 bps) in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Includes standard asset provisioning of 11% of total
GNPA -28 bps QoQ; NNPA -8 bps QoQ

segments.name: Wholesale advances
segments.commentary: Grew 56% YoY; corporate segment up 60% YoY and commercial banking up 47% YoY. Management says growth is largely working-capital driven, with no single sector standing out.

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 32% YoY. Secured retail rose 52% YoY (including about INR10,300 crores of FCNR leverage), while unsecured retail grew 11% YoY. Retail-wholesale mix is 56:44.

segments.name: Cards and microfinance (unsecured)
segments.commentary: Card book about INR19,000-20,000 crores; card provisioning about INR575 crores in the quarter, with September month slippages cited at INR125-130 crores. Microfinance is growing about 5-6% QoQ and is treated as a PSL product.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits up 34% YoY to INR1,56,272 crores, but up only 6% excluding FCNR. CASA grew 14% YoY to INR42,526 crores; average CASA ratio 24% (28.1% ex-FCNR). Term deposits crossed INR1 lakh crores at INR1,13,746 crores. FCNR EOP stock about INR32,300 crores.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected slightly lower in Q3 FY27 on a blended basis, then inching up in Q4 as the repo hike flows through; management gave no firm FY28 NIM guidance.
Card credit costs expected to fall from low double digits to about 6% (5.5-6%), with card slippages around INR400 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4.
Opex growth expected at around 7-8% in the near term, rising to low single digits or slightly higher as branch, people, wealth and technology spend increases.
Advances baseline of 22-25% growth going forward per management; analyst modelling of 5-6% QoQ was endorsed. FY27 overall loan growth expected at about 15-20%, with FY28 similar.
Cards expected to stop de-growing within a quarter and deliver high single to low double-digit growth; unsecured mix to stay around 19-20%.

Branch network target of about 1,000 branches in 2.5-3 years; around 30-50 branches to be added per quarter. ENBD India amalgamation expected to complete in FY27, subject to RBI approval. Normal LCR target 120-125%.
Bancassurance income of about INR300 crores a year could fall 50-60% if the draft IRDAI circular is implemented as drafted.
capex_capacity: Around 38 branches to open in the weeks after the call; the network is being densified and expanded at 30-50 branches per quarter.
Wealth management and NRI propositions in early stages; product and RM build-out expected to take time.

Liquidity of about 35% of balance sheet from capital raise and FCNR deposits; short-term investments and wholesale short-term loans used as tactical deployment, with full deployment expected over the medium term.
AFS book at INR43,000 crores vs INR37,700 crores in the prior quarter; management kept duration light.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances fell from 11.2% to 10.8%, which management attributed to mix (wholesale up, unsecured down) and FCNR leverage; ex-FCNR yield would be 10-15 bps higher.
Cost of TD is 6.86% (FCNR and INR combined), INR TD cost 7.12%; cost of SA about 5% after recent cuts; total cost of funds down QoQ.
Loan book on external benchmarks: about 58% (32% repo-linked, 11% FBIL, 12% other external, about 3.5-4% MCLR). Repo loans reset on 90-day cycles.
Corporate deposit rates have fallen as ratings upgrades and supply-demand shifts lower funding costs for wholesale.
Fee income up 12% YoY to INR1,040 crores; Q2 includes a one-off from the FCNR currency swap, so sequential fee growth is not repeatable.
Management said collections remain stable, with no material impact yet from the Middle East conflict or deficient monsoons in certain districts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did period-end CASA rise about 15% QoQ while average CASA was flat, and what is the retail franchise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rate cuts let go of high-cost CASA, which the team expects to recoup over 4-5 months. Branch expansion, staff densification and the affluent/wealth push, with ENBD support, are the levers; retail TDs grew about 16% this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory for Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Iyer said Q3 blended margin would be slightly lower than Q2, then inch up in Q4, depending on deployment speed of liquidity and the repo hike flowing through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the bancassurance draft circular?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca income is about INR300 crores a year; management expects a 50-60% drop if the draft is implemented as written.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cards slippage and credit cost trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Card slippages were about INR125-130 crores in September alone; card slippages are expected around INR400 crores per quarter in Q3-Q4, and card credit cost should fall from low double digits to about 6%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the liquidity improve the ROA profile and what is the FY28 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 ROA targets or three-year targets; it said current RoA is 0.92% and the next few quarters look positive. It expects tailwinds to margins and growth from fixed-rate liquidity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for wholesale sector mix, short-term lending and wealth business?
qa_highlights.answer: Wholesale growth is largely working-capital driven with no sector standing out; project finance is a small share. Wealth is at a very early stage, with no launch expected imminently.

risks_watch: Margin compression as wholesale and money-market yields dilute the book yield; the 10.8% advances yield and falling SA/TD costs need to offset each other.
CASA growth is weak (6% ex-FCNR deposit growth); a mix shift to corporate and wholesale funding may raise the cost of funds over time.
Bancassurance fee income may fall 50-60% if the IRDAI draft circular is implemented.
Monsoon deficits in some districts and the Middle East conflict could affect rural and retail collections; the bank is monitoring these.
ECL transition next year could change steady-state credit cost; management gave no mix-based estimate.
Standard asset provisioning from FCNR-funded book growth (40 bps on incremental advances) and possible FCNR run-off.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, card slippages and the liquidity tailwind, but cautious and evasive on forward targets. Management declined to give FY28 ROA, three-year targets, or firm NIM and cost-of-deposit guidance, and deferred several detailed answers to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our advances grew this quarter by 42% year-on-year to INR1,42,314 crores and average advances grew 33% year-on-year.
Cost to income ratio for the quarter was 56.5% versus 70.7% in Q2 FY26.
So, going forward, as your stage one will be the fact that we'll move from the investment yield to wholesale yield and from then wholesale yield to the blended advances yield.
We are still willing to pick up all deposits which is available at a particular price point.

adds.what: Around 38 branches to open in the weeks after the call; network densifying at 30-50 branches per quarter toward ~1,000 branches in 2.5-3 years

growth.why: Management guides FY27 loan growth of about 15-20% (midpoint ~17.5%, shown as revenue proxy 15) with a 22-25% advances baseline and opex growth of 7-8%; backing is partly specific (38 branches opening, 30-50 per quarter, wholesale working-capital demand) but no firm capacity or order numbers, and the 1,000-branch target is 2.5-3 years out.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q3 FY27 lower, Q4 FY27 up
rows.why: NIM at 4.61% (+48 bps QoQ) with management guiding slightly lower in Q3 and inching up in Q4 as the repo hike flows through; yield on advances fell 11.2% to 10.8% and no FY28 NIM guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 38 branches to open in the weeks after the call, with the network densifying at 30-50 branches per quarter toward about 1,000 branches in 2.5-3 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management sets a minimum advances growth baseline of 22-25% YoY, with FY27 loan growth guided at about 15-20%; advances were up 42% YoY to INR1,42,314 crores, though FCNR-funded and wholesale working-capital driven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; the liquidity is about 35% of the balance sheet and branch expansion is already in the 30-50 per quarter plan, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided opex growth of 7-8%, FY27 loan growth of 15-20%, and card credit cost falling to about 6%, with no raise signalled; it declined to give FY28 ROA or medium-term targets.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 margin guided slightly lower, bancassurance income of about INR300 crores a year could fall 50-60% under the draft IRDAI circular, and the ECL transition could change steady-state credit cost.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wealth and NRI propositions are at an early stage with no launch expected imminently, and no new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Bancassurance income hit from draft IRDAI circular
rows.why: Banca income of about INR300 crores a year could fall 50-60% (about INR150-180 crores) if the draft circular is implemented as written.

rows.label: Card credit cost easing toward 6%
rows.why: Card slippages guided to around INR400 crores per quarter for Q3 and Q4 versus about INR575 crores of card provisioning this quarter, with card credit cost falling from low double digits to about 6%.

rows.label: ENBD India amalgamation
rows.why: Amalgamation expected to complete in FY27 subject to RBI approval, supporting CASA and branch expansion.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, card slippages and the liquidity tailwind but cautious and evasive on forward targets, declining FY28 ROA and three-year targets; analysts pushed on margin trajectory, CASA mix and the bancassurance circular.
